## New Cross-Domain Connections

- **[2026-10-17] GLP-1 obesity drugs drive four separate paper trades, and those trades point in opposite directions. Each one treats the drugs as its own single-stock story. Health, the domain that would say whether Fred himself should care about GLP-1s, has no page on them. This month's book pick, *Off the Scales*, is the first source in the wiki on the drugs themselves.** In [[finance/paper-trading/paper-trading-portfolio]], NVO was bought in May on "GLP-1 market leadership" and closed 09-23 at −11.6% when that franchise came under pressure ([[finance/paper-trading/trades/2026-05-28-NVO]]). PEP closed 09-21 at −8.6%, and [[finance/ideas/idea-pep]] names mass GLP-1 adoption as its "primary new secular risk" to Frito-Lay volumes. AMGN is still open at +5.9%, partly on MariTide obesity optionality ([[finance/paper-trading/trades/2026-08-05-AMGN]]). The new UNH entry ([[finance/paper-trading/trades/2026-10-13-UNH]]) rests on the medical cost ratio falling (88.4%), but its risk list (MA rates, PBM reform, DOJ/Optum) never mentions GLP-1 spend, which insurers have widely cited as a medical and pharmacy cost pressure. Faster GLP-1 uptake helps AMGN and hurts PEP and, plausibly, UNH's MCR. The book is carrying one factor in both directions without ever netting it out. [[books/suggestions]] (October) adds Donnellan's *Off the Scales*, the Novo/Lilly story from the lab onward. Meanwhile [[health/my-protocol]]'s Diet section is still blank and [[health/source-wood-brain-sharp-2026]] is silent on GLP-1s, despite Health's men-~50 scope. Next step: add "GLP-1 uptake" as a named variable to the UNH thesis before the January Q4 check, alongside MCR.

## New Investigation Ideas

- **[2026-10-13] Nearly every price bug the live-portfolio pipeline has had is a units or listing bug: wrong currency, wrong exchange, or pence read as pounds. AI & Tech's Unity page already sets out the fix Fred uses in his game, a fast test tier that runs on every change. The Finance scripts have no equivalent.** The bugs are all on record. EDEN was routed to an unrelated US ticker and showed +320% instead of −0.45% (memory/index.md Key Decisions, 07-28). The Options "Mkt Value (€)" column copied native-USD marks as EUR and overstated net value by ~€172 twice before anyone noticed (09-22). ACN needed the Xetra CSA listing, not an ACN.xx suffix (08-04). KLR's entry price needed correcting (2,418p → 2,400p). On 10-08 [[finance/trading-portfolio]] notes that Last Price and P&L% "were updated by hand". [[ai-tech/unity-development-with-claude-code]] rule 5 is the opposite discipline: a plain core tested "in seconds on every change", backed by an engine-free design that bans `float` game state so a units mistake can't compile silently. It was written for [[games/project-terrain-autobattler]]. These are bugs a lookup table catches. None of them needs judgment. Concrete step: add a ~20-line pre-flight check to the portfolio-management-briefing pipeline that pins one known-good reference row per listing type (an EUR Euronext name like EDEN.PA, a GBp LSE name like KLR.L, CSA.DE, one USD option mark) and checks currency, price order of magnitude (within ±50% of the last verified close) and EUR conversion before the briefing is written. The run should fail loudly instead of publishing. It is cheaper than the next reconciliation pass and follows the same rule Fred already wrote for himself in the game.

## New Cross-Domain Connections

- **[2026-10-13] Fred's best live holding, Keller Group (KLR, +35%, already free-ridden), has quietly become an AI data-centre construction play. The portfolio's risk table still files it as "European value — no signal", and its thesis lists only US housing as a risk. AI & Tech's data-centre delay sources bear directly on it, and in the opposite direction from Fred's ORCL/PLTR/NBIS puts.** The thesis in [[finance/source-magic-formula-ftse250-screen-2026]] (May, ~2,090p) is a Magic Formula pick: ~17% earnings yield, ~20% ROIC, risks "US residential construction slowdown; commodity cost exposure". Keller's H1 2026 results (outside source, not yet in the wiki) changed the mix. Data centres became the group's largest subsector at 9% of revenue, up from 3% in 2025. Keller finished more data-centre projects in H1 than in all of 2025. North America revenue rose 16.7%, the board said full-year results will be "materially ahead" of consensus, and the shares hit a record. That is most of the move to 3,264p. [[finance/trading-portfolio]]'s Burry-lens table still groups KLR with GSK and EDEN as "no signal". Foundations are the first trade on a site, so Keller earns only from projects that have site control and are physically being built. That is the layer [[ai-tech/source-semianalysis-datacenter-delay-narrative-2026-06-18]] says is real, as opposed to the announcement-only pipeline that makes up most "cancelled" headlines. Two things follow. (1) Keller is the AI-capex risk Fred can actually measure: the [[ai-tech/source-dc-capex-build-costs-2026]] estimate that 30–50% of 2026 capacity slips to 2028, or a spread of [[ai-tech/source-trump-ai-executive-order-gold-eagle-2026-07-19]]-style state moratoria, would hit Keller's newest growth line first. (2) Fred's book is less hedged against an AI-capex bust than the table suggests: the puts profit from the same slowdown that would de-rate his biggest winner. This is a sibling of the 10-12 EOG connection, but EOG is a candidate; KLR is a held position with real gains at stake. Next step: change KLR's risk-table row to "🟡 AI-capex beneficiary (data-centre foundations ~9% of revenue)", add data-centre slippage to the thesis's risk list, and use the H2 trading update as the dated test (is data-centre share still rising, or did the order book roll over?).
